h1: Large format printing planned at full scale
lead: Large format printing turns artwork into physical graphics that may be viewed across a room, along a storefront or at the scale of a wall. That change in scale affects image quality, typography and finishing. Vision Graphics helps New York businesses prepare the project around the final use rather than simply enlarging a file. Share the intended dimensions, viewing conditions and display method so the artwork, material and production layout can be reviewed together before the job moves into print.

sections.h2: Prepare the file for the finished size
sections.html: Review image resolution, crop, fonts and color references in the context of the final output. A digital preview cannot show every material or lighting effect. Identify where proofing or a sample would help resolve a meaningful design decision.

The final use determines whether the graphic needs trimming, paneling, hems, attachment details or another finish. Oversized work may require a coordinated panel sequence and access planning. Confirm the substrate or display hardware before artwork dimensions are locked.

items.a_html: Files need evaluation at the intended output size and viewing distance. The original image is more useful than a compressed copy.
Include dimensions, quantity, use location, display method and any brand color references or finishing requirements.
